# freshdesk_automation_rule (Resource)

An automation rule: a dispatcher (`rule_type = 1`), a time-triggered rule (`3`), or an observer (`4`).

-> The rule body is given as JSON because Freshdesk's condition and action shapes depend on the fields they reference. Build them with `jsonencode`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A dispatcher rule (rule_type 1) that routes urgent tickets to a group.
resource "freshdesk_automation_rule" "urgent_to_billing" {
  rule_type = 1
  name      = "Route urgent billing tickets"
  active    = true

  conditions = jsonencode([
    {
      name       = "condition_set_1"
      match_type = "all"
      properties = [
        {
          resource_type = "ticket"
          field_name    = "priority"
          operator      = "in"
          value         = [4]
        },
      ]
    },
  ])

  actions = jsonencode([
    { field_name = "group_id", value = freshdesk_group.billing.id },
  ])
}

resource "freshdesk_group" "billing" {
  name = "Billing"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the rule.
- `rule_type` (Number) Which automation the rule belongs to: `1` ticket creation (dispatcher), `3` time triggers, `4` ticket updates (observer). Changing it forces a new rule.

### Optional

- `actions` (String) Actions as a JSON array. Each element takes `field_name` and `value`, plus an optional `email` object for email actions.
- `active` (Boolean) Whether the rule is running.
- `conditions` (String) Condition sets as a JSON array. Each element takes `name` (`condition_set_1` or `condition_set_2`), `match_type` (`all` or `any`) and a `properties` array.
- `description` (String) Description of the rule.
- `events` (String) Field changes an observer rule watches, as a JSON array of objects.
- `operator` (String) How the condition sets combine: `AND` or `OR`.
- `performer` (String) Who must act for an observer rule to fire, as a JSON object, for example `jsonencode({ type = 1 })`.
- `position` (Number) Evaluation order within the automation.

### Read-Only

- `affected_tickets_count` (Number) How many tickets the rule has acted on.
- `created_at` (String) When the rule was created (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Numeric identifier of the rule.
- `outdated` (Boolean) Whether the rule references a field that no longer exists, which stops it firing.
- `updated_at` (String) When the rule was last changed (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import as <rule_type>:<rule_id>, where rule_type is 1, 3 or 4.
terraform import freshdesk_automation_rule.example 1:109866
```
